description.value: This study investigated the discontinuity hypothesis using fMRI by examining cortical activation during encoding of emotional faces as a function of repressive versus sensitizing coping style.

spans.text: This study investigates the discontinuity hypothesis using functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI).

value: Repressors are expected to evaluate emotional faces as less threatening than sensitizers.
repressors will show an increased response to threatening faces (i.e. angry and fearful facial expression) in cortical regions which are known to play a role in emotion regulation and memory encoding
repressors' memory for threatening faces should be better directly after encoding compared to that of sensitizers.
repressors will show a decreased memory for threatening faces after three days compared to sensitizers.
